summary: A University of Findlay Online article examines the "sandwich approach" (compliment sandwich or hamburger method) to giving employee feedback, where negative criticism sits between two positives. It lists arguments for the technique, such as softening harsh comments, and against it, such as undermining criticism and teaching employees to distrust praise. The article contrasts constructive and destructive criticism and closes by promoting the university's fully online MBA program.
one_line: Overview of the pros and cons of the sandwich feedback method and the difference between constructive and destructive criticism, from the University of Findlay Online.
key_facts: The "sandwich approach" or "hamburger method" places a piece of negative feedback between two positive ones.
Supporters say the sandwich approach may ease the sting of hearing difficult comments.
Lyuba Konopasek, MD, and Miriam Bar-on, MD, describe a medical-field method called "Ask-Tell-Ask".
In Ask-Tell-Ask, supervisors ask subordinates to evaluate their own work practices and methods of improvement.
An evaluation done by the Journal of Behavioral Studies in Business found the sandwich method can be damaging.
One criticism is that the method trains employees to distrust praise because they anticipate the criticism that follows.
The article says the sandwich approach can be wildly inappropriate for major breaches of trust or safety concerns.
Psychology Today is cited as explaining the distinction between constructive and destructive criticism.
Constructive criticism emphasizes results and discusses specific problem areas rather than attacking the whole person.
Destructive criticism often makes judgments, accusations, and exaggerations and may discuss things that aren't changeable, such as an employee's essential personality.
Constructive criticism is more likely to lead to self-reflection, while destructive criticism is more likely to lead to unhelpful blaming.
The University of Findlay's online MBA program is offered fully online to accommodate working professionals.
The University of Findlay is located at 1000 N Main St., Findlay, OH 45840.
